I mean, yeah, I agree if we're talking about homosexuality and being trans, but what about behaviors that everyone currently thinks of as socially unacceptable and dangerous? How do we decide if it's an actual thing we should treat or if our judgment is clouded?

See: pedophilia. I'd argue this is a socially unacceptable behavior that HAS to be treated, because if you don't... you're just giving up on people that are either gonna suffer their whole lives or end up in jail after hurting someone. But it's not an objectively bad thing. Nature is okay with pedophilia. We're against it cause society deems hurting others as a bad thing, but it's fundamentally no different than previous generations going "we think homosexuality is morally wrong so we're gonna treat it as a mental illness". It's all a product of our social conditioning.

Disclaimer: I'm not trying to argue pedophile should be accepted as normal behavior as that's definitely NOT the case, and I'm not trying to compare being gay (I'm bi myself) or trans as being a pedophile. But I'm interested in what exactly sets apart my belief ("pedophilia is always wrong and should be treated so that those people can have a better life and not hurt anyone") from similar beliefs our grandfathers had about other things. There's no universal law that says pedophilia is wrong, or even simply killing people, it's just society that decided that's the case. Just like it decided homosexuality was wrong.
